## AI-Generated Fix (javascript)

```javascript
const express = require('express');
const app = express();
const port = 8882;

// Middleware to sanitize user input
const sanitizeInput = (req, res, next) => {
  for (let key in req.body) {
    if (typeof req.body[key] === 'string') {
      req.body[key] = req.body[key].replace(/</g, '&lt;').replace(/>/g, '&gt;');
    }
  }
  next();
};

app.use(express.json());
app.use(sanitizeInput);

app.post('/', (req, res) => {
  // Process the sanitized input
  res.send(`Received input: ${req.body.input}`);
});

app.listen(port, () => {
  console.log(`Server running at http://34.16.47.248:${port}`);
});
```

---

## Explanation

The vulnerability was due to unsanitized user input being rendered directly in the web application, allowing for potential XSS attacks. The fix involves adding a middleware function that sanitizes user input by escaping HTML special characters, preventing malicious scripts from being executed in the browser.
